sections.body: Governments collect TAXES to pay for public services: roads, schools, hospitals, defence. Common types: income tax, sales tax/VAT/GST, and property tax.
Many countries use PROGRESSIVE income tax: higher rates apply to higher portions of income.
A PAYSLIP shows GROSS pay (before deductions) and NET pay (take-home), plus deductions like income tax, social security/pension contributions.
Rules differ a lot by country. Use official government websites to learn yours.

hints: Think of what lands in your bank account.
If gross pay is 1,000 and deductions are 150, what you actually receive is 850. What's that called?
quiz.explain: Net pay is what you take home after tax and other deductions.

quiz.q: A VAT/GST is a tax on…
hints: It's added to prices in shops.
Income tax is taken from wages. Which tax is taken when you buy things?
quiz.explain: VAT/GST is a tax on goods and services when you buy them.

quiz.q: In a made-up progressive tax system, the first 10,000 of income is taxed at 0% and any income above 10,000 is taxed at 20%. How much income tax does someone earning 25,000 pay?
hints: Only the part of income ABOVE 10,000 is taxed at 20%.
Work out how much of the 25,000 is above 10,000, then take 20% of that part only.
Worked example: if the first 5,000 is taxed at 0% and anything above at 10%, someone earning 12,000 pays 10% of 7,000 = 700.
quiz.explain: The first 10,000 is tax-free. The remaining 15,000 is taxed at 20%: 0.2 × 15,000 = 3,000. In a progressive system the higher rate applies only to the portion of income above the threshold, not to all of it (that mistake gives 5,000). Real tax bands differ by country.
